fix.shows: Aman Bhargava of Diagram Chasing tests the line printed on every page of the Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer's summary booklet for the final roll, that no eligible citizen is left out and no ineligible person is included, against the rolls themselves. He read all 60,923 booth files of the final roll of 27 October by machine and joined them by EPIC number to digitised copies of the 2002 roll, the January 2025 roll, the list of names left off the draft and the notice lists, which the groups Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka made. He reports that of 1,05,48,148 electors left off the draft whom he found on the January 2025 roll, about 14,900 came back on the final roll in the same constituency with the same name, relative and age, and that 206 of 8.9 lakh aged 75 and over came back. He counts 3,115 electors told they were not on the 2002 roll although the Chief Electoral Officer's own copy of it carries them under the same EPIC number, 4,954 deleted after a notice that flagged children born less than nine months apart, a rule that catches twins, 8,992 people on the roll more than once in their own booth, 461 EPIC numbers on the roll in two constituencies and 234 new voters in Dasarahalli given an EPIC number held earlier by someone left off the draft. He finds the share of electors sent a notice ranging from 0.03 per cent in Mayakonda to 59 per cent in C.V. Raman Nagar, and nine constituencies where no notice ended in a finding of ineligibility. He says his counts are minimums, that the rolls by themselves cannot establish identity, and that the work rests on optical character recognition of files the Commission publishes as PDFs.

note: Second reading, 13 November 2026, of the page fetched with curl and read as text. Title, outlet, the byline (Aman Bhargava) and the date (November 12, 2026) match. Checked against the page: 60,923 booth PDFs read by OCR, the joins by voter ID to the 2002, January 2025 and draft rolls, the pre-draft deletions and the notices digitised by Mathakaavalu and Edellu Karnataka, 1,05,48,148 found on the January 2025 roll, about 14,900 back in the same constituency matched on name, relative and age, 206 of 8.9 lakh aged 75 and over, 3,115, 4,954, 8,992, 461, 234 in Dasarahalli, 0.03 per cent in Mayakonda, 59 per cent in C.V. Raman Nagar and nine constituencies with no finding of ineligibility. Both quotes are verbatim. Three changes to shows. The footer is on every page of the Chief Electoral Officer's summary booklet, so the sentence names the booklet. The author's caveat is that the rolls by themselves cannot conclusively establish identity, so the sentence now says that instead of attributing it to the name match alone. The page says the Commission publishes the data as PDFs, and it also refers to the CEO's published CSV of the 2002 roll, so 'only' was removed. The first reading's note stands: no individual voter is named here, and no booth PDF or row-level dataset link was opened or carried.
